explanation: Western visitors often treat a thumbs-up as universally positive, but established UAE business-etiquette guidance specifically warns against it (grouped with crossing your legs) as a gesture that can cause offence. At the same time, decades of Western media exposure mean many Emiratis, especially younger ones, now read it as simply 'good' or 'OK', so the real-world reaction is genuinely inconsistent.
local_tip: In business settings or with older Emiratis, use a verbal thank-you or a nod instead of a thumbs-up.

also_check.note: The thumbs-up is widely considered an obscene insult, roughly equivalent to the middle finger elsewhere.
The gesture generally reads as positive, though it carries no special emphasis the way a wai does.
Older Greeks in particular may read an abrupt thumbs-up as closer to a rude dismissal than a compliment.

sources.title: Culture and etiquette tips when doing business in the UAE
